newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AWB sees China as possible buyer, India uncertain.
newsitem.headline: AWB sees China as possible buyer, India uncertain.

text.p: China could be in the market for wheat later this year but no sales were being planned at present, the Australian Wheat Board (AWB) told Reuters on Wednesday.
Chinese demand for imported wheat was down because of its strong current crop, the AWB said.
But later, if China showed itself to be an active buyer on international markets, the AWB said it expected it would be one of the main parties negotiating sales.
The AWB was commenting on reports from another news agency quoting chairman Trevor Flugge as saying that the board was likely to secure a major buy order from China in the next three or four months.

Flugge, visiting China as part of a delegation headed by Australian prime minister John Howard, said any orders were unlikely to match the sale of 2.23 million tonnes to China in the year ended June 30 1996.
Australia expected to gain a fair percentage of an expected expanding market in China in coming years for wheat and other grains, Flugge was quoted as saying.
The USDA forecasts China's 1997 wheat production at 110.0 million tonnes, up from 108.0 million tonnes in 1996 and 102.2 million tonnes in 1995.
Chinese import demand for wheat in 1997/98 has been put at six million tonnes and in 1996/97 at four million tonnes, a significant drop from earlier projections.
The AWB also told Reuters that Indian wheat demand was unknown as that country's harvest approached.
This statement follows India's deferral of a decision on wheat imports beyond an earlier-authorised two million tonnes.
International grain sources recently believed that India had contracted to import a further one million tonnes of wheat from Australia for August, November and December shipments.
